nodes.title: Compact manifolds without boundary, smooth complex vector bundles, and sections
nodes.statement: X is a finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold; in the main index theorems X is compact and has no boundary. E and F are smooth complex vector bundles of finite rank, and Γ(E) denotes the smooth sections. Auxiliary open manifolds carry an additional finite-topological-type hypothesis.

nodes.title: Hermitian metrics, the L² pairing, and formal adjoints
nodes.statement: A Riemannian density and Hermitian bundle metrics define the L² pairing by integration. The formal adjoint P* of a differential operator is characterized by (Pu,v)=(u,P*v). On a closed manifold the identity holds for arbitrary smooth sections; on an open manifold it is initially stated for compactly supported sections. Densities allow X to be nonorientable.

nodes.title: Differential operators, principal symbols, and ellipticity
nodes.statement: In local coordinates, use D_j=−i∂/∂x_j and write P=Σ_{|α|≤m} a_α(x)D^α. Its principal symbol is σ_m(P)(x,ξ)=Σ_{|α|=m} a_α(x)ξ^α, an m-homogeneous bundle map π*E→π*F. Ellipticity means that this map is invertible for every nonzero covector ξ; no invertibility condition is imposed on the zero section.

nodes.title: Sobolev spaces Hˢ(E) of bundle sections
nodes.statement: For a finite-rank smooth bundle E over a compact manifold X without boundary, local squared Sobolev norms are defined by ∫(1+|ξ|²)^s|û(ξ)|²dξ and assembled with finitely many trivializations and a partition of unity before completion. The order s is real. For nonnegative integral orders, covariant-derivative norms give equivalent norms. Independence of the chosen presentation is the content of A01.

nodes.title: Symbol classes, pseudodifferential operators, and the SG classical subclass
nodes.statement: Local symbols in S^m_{1,0} satisfy |∂_x^α∂_ξ^β a(x,ξ)|≤C_{K,α,β}(1+|ξ|)^{m−|β|} on each compact coordinate set K. The principal symbol is taken modulo S^{m−1}. The classical convention in SG requires a representative of this principal symbol homogeneous near infinity; it does not require a homogeneous expansion at every lower order.

references.locator: III.13, definition of classical operators and equation (13.5)

nodes.title: Fredholm operators and the integer index
nodes.statement: A bounded complex-linear operator T:H₁→H₂ between complex Hilbert spaces is Fredholm when its kernel and cokernel are finite-dimensional and its range is closed. Its index is ind T=dim_ℂ ker T−dim_ℂ coker T. In this situation coker T is isomorphic to ker T*, where T* is the bounded Hilbert-space adjoint. Relating this adjoint to the formal adjoint of a differential operator is a separate comparison.

nodes.title: K-groups and relative and compactly supported triple models
nodes.statement: For compact Hausdorff X, K⁰(X) is the group completion of the direct-sum monoid of finite-rank complex vector bundles. If A⊆X is closed, a relative class in K⁰(X,A) is represented by [E,F;α] with α:E|A≅F|A, modulo stabilization and relative homotopy. For locally compact Hausdorff Y, K_c⁰(Y)=K̃⁰(Y⁺); a supporting triple is invertible outside a compact set, and its homotopies have a common compact support bound.

references.locator: II.1.26–1.29; LCH compact-support extension is a project supplement

nodes.title: Principal bundles, associated bundles, representation rings, and equivariant K-classes
nodes.statement: A compact Lie group G acts compatibly on the base and bundle. R(G) is the Grothendieck ring of finite-dimensional complex representations, and equivariant K-groups have an equivariant bundle-triple model. A principal G-bundle P₀→X induces a_P₀:R(G)→K(X), sending [V] to [P₀×_G V].

nodes.title: Differential forms and the de Rham complex
nodes.statement: Ωᵖ(X) is the space of smooth p-forms, the exterior derivative satisfies d²=0, and de Rham cohomology is ker d/im d. A metric determines d* and the Hodge Laplacian. The sphere model in the index argument uses these objects independently of characteristic classes.

nodes.title: Bott elements, K-orientations, and complex Thom elements
nodes.statement: The Hermitian exterior-algebra model [π*Λeven E,π*Λodd E; v∧−ι_v*] defines the complex Bott and Thom classes. Over compact bases, a K-orientation is a class generating K_c(E) as a free rank-one K(X)-module. For locally finite-rank complex bundles over locally compact Hausdorff bases with a supplied continuous Hermitian metric, the specified degree-zero compact-support Thom operator has metric independence, proper and open naturality, ordered direct-sum compatibility, and the compact zero-section convention.
nodes.literature_statement: Over a compact base, a K-orientation generates K_c(E) as a free rank-one K(X)-module. The candidate for a complex bundle is [π*Λeven E,π*Λodd E; v∧−ι_v*]. Over a noncompact base, its fiberwise compact-support Thom class multiplies compactly supported base classes.
nodes.scope_boundary: The noncompact interface is degree zero and uses a supplied continuous Hermitian metric. It does not assert that every complex bundle over an arbitrary locally compact Hausdorff base admits such a metric, nor does it assert real or spin orientations or all negative-degree noncompact Thom operators.

nodes.title: Singular cohomology, characteristic classes, and compact-support pairings
nodes.statement: Use singular cohomology together with relative and compactly supported cohomology. The integral Euler class is defined for oriented real bundles, Chern classes for complex bundles, and Pontryagin classes for real bundles; the index formulas use their images over ℚ. On noncompact TX, pair H_c^*(TX;ℚ) with the oriented locally finite fundamental class rather than an ordinary top-dimensional fundamental class.

nodes.title: Smooth geometric foundations and relative constructions
nodes.statement: Smooth geometry provides finite coordinate covers on compact manifolds, smooth partitions of unity, metrics and connections, relative extension, Euclidean embeddings of compact manifolds, tubular neighborhoods, and homotopy control for the relevant choices.

references.locator: Uses in III.2, III.12, and III.13
Chapter 18, Remark 10.5: a referral to Whitney, not a proof

nodes.title: Fourier analysis and Hilbert and Banach space foundations
nodes.statement: The analytic foundations include Fourier inversion and Plancherel, completions and duality, the open-mapping and bounded-inverse theorems, compact-operator properties, and finite-dimensional rank formulas.

references.locator: III.2, Fourier foundations; III.7, functional analysis

nodes.title: Compact-support duality, Gysin maps, and pairings
nodes.statement: For the oriented manifolds under consideration, compact-support Poincaré duality, extension by zero and integration, and the Thom–Gysin relations for the zero section and bundle projection are compatible. The relevant locally finite and compact-support versions apply to noncompact tangent total spaces.

references.locator: §3.3, Lemmas 3.27 and 3.36 and Theorem 3.35; integral orientation and Poincaré duality

nodes.scope_boundary: The specified duality uses singular cohomology over ℚ, obtained from compatible integral local orientation generators, and the native tangent-bundle Thom–Gysin comparisons. General differential-form or independent frame-model comparisons are separate mathematical variants.

nodes.title: An independent foundation for the Bott theorem
nodes.statement: Multiplication by the specified positive complex-line Bott class gives an isomorphism K_c⁰(Y)→K_c⁰(Y×ℂ) for locally compact Hausdorff Y. The prescribed degree-zero relative Bott product is an isomorphism for compact Hausdorff closed pairs and the required compact parameter pairs. The Bott argument is independent of the target Atiyah–Singer index theorems.

references.locator: III.1.3–1.4 and the beginning of the proof

nodes.literature_statement: Complex Bott multiplication is an isomorphism, with relative and parameter formulations. Karoubi III.1.3 also states nonpositive graded and locally compact relative versions.
nodes.scope_boundary: The specified relative interface is degree zero on compact Hausdorff closed pairs. It does not assert a noncompact ordinary-relative K-group carrier or all nonpositive graded Bott operators. Noncompact closed pairs are treated through compactly supported K-theory of their open complements.
scope_constraints: Parameter classes have joint compact-support control on the full product; pointwise compact support is insufficient.
Proper pullback and extension along open inclusions are distinct operations preserving the same specified positive Bott class.

nodes.title: Equivariant averaging and realization of equivariant symbols
nodes.statement: Averaging over compact groups supplies invariant metrics and equivariant quantizations. The equivariant K-classes used in the argument admit smooth representatives and equivariant elliptic-operator realizations, with the specified bundles and compact-support control.

references.locator: III.13.6, equivariant operator representatives and lifting

nodes.title: De Rham cohomology of spheres and the natural group action
nodes.statement: For r≥1, H⁰_dR(Sʳ;ℂ)≅ℂ and Hʳ_dR(Sʳ;ℂ)≅ℂ, and the other groups vanish. Under the O(r) action g↦diag(g,1), H⁰ is the trivial representation and Hʳ is the determinant representation; the equivariant de Rham index is therefore 1+(−1)^r det. S⁰ has two components and is treated as two points.

references.locator: II.5.15 and its use in III.13.7
§2.2, degree of reflections and orientation action on sphere homology

nodes.title: Clifford representations and spin Thom generators
nodes.statement: The spin branch uses irreducible graded complex Clifford representations, their compatible spinor modules, and the identification of the corresponding Clifford symbol with the complex Bott generator.

references.locator: I.1–5 and the use of I.9.27

nodes.title: Complementary bundles, pullbacks, and homotopy invariance
nodes.statement: A finite-rank vector bundle over a compact Hausdorff base has a finite-rank complementary bundle. Homotopic maps f₀,f₁:A→B with paracompact A induce isomorphic pullback bundles f₀*E≅f₁*E. Smooth and relative versions retain the specified trivializations outside a fixed compact set.

nodes.title: Triple models, extension by zero, external products, and Mayer–Vietoris
nodes.statement: The bundle-triple models agree with relative and compactly supported K-groups. Direct sum, stabilization, external products, and extension along open inclusions satisfy the corresponding naturality identities, and the relative theory has Mayer–Vietoris long exact sequences.

references.locator: IV.1, compatibility of extension by zero in the proof
II.1.26–1.29; LCH compact-support extension is a project supplement

nodes.title: Complex Bott periodicity and Euclidean normalization
nodes.statement: For the locally compact Hausdorff spaces Y used here, external multiplication by the specified complex Bott class gives K_c⁰(Y)≅K_c⁰(Y×ℂᴺ). In particular K_c⁰(ℂᴺ)≅ℤ. The generator and its sign agree with the exterior-algebra model in D10.

references.locator: III.1, Theorems 1.3 and 1.4 and the complete §1 proof

nodes.title: The Thom isomorphism for complex vector bundles
nodes.statement: For a locally finite-rank complex bundle π:V→X over a locally compact Hausdorff base with a supplied jointly continuous Hermitian metric, the specified degree-zero map u↦π*u·λ_V is an isomorphism K_c⁰(X)→K_c⁰(V). It is independent of the supplied metric. A paracompact Hausdorff base admits such a metric.
nodes.literature_statement: For a complex vector bundle V→X, the Thom class λ_V gives u↦π*u·λ_V as a compact-support Thom isomorphism K_c(X)→K_c(V), interpreted using fiberwise compact support where appropriate.
nodes.scope_boundary: The specified interface is degree zero with a supplied jointly continuous Hermitian metric. Metric existence for arbitrary locally compact Hausdorff bases without paracompactness is not part of the statement.

nodes.title: Tangent-bundle pushforward for embeddings
nodes.statement: For a smooth proper embedding f:X→Y of Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifolds with full finite-dimensional real models, the normal bundle of Tf identifies with π*(ν⊕ν). Its specified complex structure, the Thom map, and extension through a tubular neighborhood define f!:K_c⁰(TX)→K_c⁰(TY). This degree-zero pushforward is independent of auxiliary choices, respects composition and identity, commutes with extension along open inclusions and standard Euclidean stabilization, and satisfies the compact-support coefficient projection formula.
nodes.scope_boundary: Changing the embedding itself is covered by K06. A projection formula for unrestricted ordinary bundle K-coefficients is a separate variant; this interface uses the compact-support coefficient formula.

nodes.title: The topological index and independence of the Euclidean embedding
nodes.statement: For compact Hausdorff second-countable smooth X without boundary, choose a Euclidean embedding f:X↪ℝᴺ and define ind_t=β_N⁻¹∘f! on K_c⁰(TX). Euclidean embeddings exist; the index is unchanged by stabilization in both coordinate blocks and by replacement of the embedding. It is natural for the specified tangent pushforwards.

references.locator: III.13, Definition 13.1 and the following discussion

nodes.scope_boundary: Embedding independence is stated for compact source manifolds. General noncompact embedding independence and sharp Whitney dimension bounds are separate statements.

nodes.title: Equivalence of Sobolev norms, embedding, compactness, and duality
nodes.statement: On a compact n-manifold X without boundary, Hˢ(E) is independent of the chosen good presentation up to equivalence of norms. If k≥0 is integral and s>n/2+k, then Hˢ(E) embeds continuously in Cᵏ(E). If s>t, the inclusion Hˢ(E)→Hᵗ(E) is compact. The L² pairing identifies Hˢ(E) and H⁻ˢ(E) as dual spaces, and a differential operator of order m extends boundedly Hˢ(E)→Hˢ⁻ᵐ(F).

nodes.title: Symbol calculus and global pseudodifferential operators
nodes.statement: The S^m_{1,0} calculus has asymptotic summation, composition, adjoint, and coordinate-change formulas, with principal symbols transforming as the corresponding bundle maps. On a compact manifold without boundary, an order-m bundle pseudodifferential operator extends boundedly Hˢ(E)→Hˢ⁻ᵐ(F), and smoothing remainders gain arbitrarily many Sobolev orders. Noncompact versions carry proper-support or localization conditions.

nodes.title: Homogeneous-symbol realization and quantization of homotopies
nodes.statement: On a compact manifold without boundary, a smooth bundle map on the unit cosphere bundle extends to a symbol homogeneous of order m near infinity and is quantized as an SG classical operator. Smooth parameter families can use a common finite cover, partition of unity, and cutoff. Continuous families use a topology controlling symbol seminorms sufficiently to give operator-norm continuity Hˢ→Hˢ⁻ᵐ.

nodes.title: Parametrices for elliptic operators
nodes.statement: An order-m elliptic bundle pseudodifferential operator P on a compact manifold without boundary has an order-−m parametrix Q for which QP−1 and PQ−1 are smoothing operators. On open manifolds the local or properly supported version applies; it alone does not imply a global Fredholm theorem.

nodes.title: Compactness of smoothing remainders
nodes.statement: On a compact manifold without boundary, every smoothing bundle operator is compact Hˢ(E)→Hˢ(F) for every real s. The factorization through a higher Sobolev order and a Rellich inclusion gives this compactness.

references.locator: III.5, opening discussion; errata sheet, item 4

nodes.title: Elliptic regularity and Fredholm Sobolev extensions
nodes.statement: On a compact manifold X without boundary, an order-m elliptic bundle pseudodifferential operator P:Hˢ(E)→Hˢ⁻ᵐ(F) is Fredholm for every real s. Locally, if a distributional section u has Pu smooth on an open set, then u is smooth there. Consequently the global weak kernels of P and its formal adjoint consist of smooth sections.

nodes.title: Independence of the analytic index from the Sobolev order
nodes.statement: For an elliptic operator on a compact manifold X without boundary, ind P=dim_ℂ ker P−dim_ℂ ker P*, with kernels on smooth sections and P* the formal adjoint. This equals the Fredholm index of every extension Hˢ(E)→Hˢ⁻ᵐ(F) and is independent of s and the auxiliary metrics.

nodes.title: Local constancy of the Fredholm index and symbol-homotopy invariance
nodes.statement: A norm-continuous Fredholm path between fixed Hilbert spaces has constant index. On a compact manifold without boundary, a smooth homotopy of elliptic symbols of fixed order, or a symbol homotopy with a continuous quantization of this kind, preserves the index. Pointwise continuity of symbols alone does not supply this hypothesis.

nodes.title: Order reduction preserving the symbol K-class and index
nodes.statement: Invertible powers of a suitable positive elliptic operator change the order of a symbol representative to zero or one while preserving its asymptotic symbol K-class and analytic index.

references.locator: XII.1.3 and the discussion of square roots
1.6 Lemma1.6.3: elliptic self-adjoint bundle spectral data; inverse/compactness route only

nodes.title: Homogeneous representatives pulled back from base bundles
nodes.statement: For a real vector bundle π:B→X over a smooth manifold X without boundary and of finite topological type, each class in K_c⁰(B) has a representative [π*E,π*F;α] with E and F trivialized outside some compact C⊂X. Off the zero section, α is invertible and homogeneous of degree zero in the fibers; over π⁻¹(X∖C) it is the identity in those trivializations. A cutoff near the compact support gives its representative across the zero section.

nodes.title: The analytic index as a homomorphism on K_c(T*X)
nodes.statement: For compact X, define ind_a,X(u)=ind P using an elliptic classical representative P of u∈K_c(T*X). The value is independent of the representative, stabilization, homotopy, and order, and is additive under direct sum.

references.locator: III.3 Observation 3.6, Corollary 3.7, Definition 3.15; III.13 (13.7)–(13.8). Component assembly and open-submanifold adapters are project supplements.

nodes.title: Excision for the analytic index
nodes.statement: If an open manifold U of finite topological type embeds openly in two compact manifolds, then a class u∈K_c(T*U) has the same analytic index after extension to either manifold.

nodes.title: Multiplicativity of the index under external products
nodes.statement: For compact X and Y, ind_a,X×Y(u⊠v)=ind_a,X(u)·ind_a,Y(v).

nodes.title: The equivariant analytic index and its homotopy invariance
nodes.statement: Let a compact Lie group G act smoothly on a compact manifold X without boundary and on its complex bundles. The kernel and cokernel of a G-equivariant elliptic operator are finite-dimensional complex G-representations, and ind_G(P)=[ker P]−[coker P]∈R(G). A norm-continuous equivariant Fredholm homotopy between fixed G-Hilbert modules preserves this representation-valued index.

nodes.title: Twisted index multiplicativity for sphere bundles
nodes.statement: Let X be compact without boundary, P₀→X a smooth principal O(r)-bundle, and Z=P₀×_{O(r)}Sʳ. For u∈K_c(T*X) and v∈K_{O(r),c}(T*Sʳ), ind_a,Z(u·v)=ind_a,X(u·a_P₀(ind_{O(r)}v)), where a_P₀:R(O(r))→K(X) is the associated-bundle map. The right side is a twisted base index and is generally not a product of two integer indices.

nodes.title: Hodge decomposition and the kernel of the de Rham operator
nodes.statement: On a compact Riemannian manifold without boundary, ker(d+d*)=ker Δ and Ωᵖ=ℋᵖ⊕dΩᵖ⁻¹⊕d*Ωᵖ⁺¹ is an L²-orthogonal decomposition, with ℋᵖ≅Hᵖ_dR. Defining d* using a metric density does not require orientation; an expression using the ordinary Hodge star adds an orientation.

nodes.title: The equivariant sphere Bott index
nodes.statement: For r≥1, let O(r) act on Sʳ by g↦diag(g,1). Either fixed-point inclusion i:pt↪Sʳ satisfies ind_{O(r)}(i!1)=1∈R(O(r)), for the specified complex Thom convention. The independent normalization in ASI supplies the argument; the representation calculation and cancellation printed in SG on p.253 cannot be used verbatim. For r=0, the inclusion picks one of the two points of S⁰, and point normalization with direct-sum additivity gives the same result.

nodes.title: Compatibility of the analytic index with embedding pushforward
nodes.statement: An embedding f:X↪Y of compact smooth manifolds satisfies ind_a,Y(f!u)=ind_a,X(u).

references.locator: III.13, Property 2 and the concluding argument

nodes.title: Normalization of the analytic index at a point
nodes.statement: Under K(pt)≅ℤ, ind_a,pt([ℂʳ]−[ℂˢ])=r−s.

nodes.title: The Atiyah–Singer K-theoretic index equality
nodes.statement: A complex elliptic pseudodifferential operator P of real order between finite-rank smooth complex bundles on a compact smooth manifold without boundary satisfies ind_a(P)=ind_t([sigma(P)]). Here [sigma(P)] is the intrinsic compact-support K-class of its full elliptic symbol.

references.locator: Derivation of the theorem from Properties 1–2

scope_constraints: The same original symbol K-class and embedding pushforward enter the analytic and topological sides.
Compactness and absence of boundary are part of the theorem; no positivity of dimension, connectedness, nonempty-base, or equal source-target rank assumption is added.
nodes.source_scope_relation: Standard ellipticity suffices. Auxiliary analytic choices and the same-operator full-symbol evaluation are supplied internally.

nodes.title: The splitting principle and universal characteristic-class calculations
nodes.statement: Pullback to a suitable flag bundle is injective on cohomology and splits the pulled-back complex bundle as a sum of line bundles. Natural characteristic classes can therefore be computed using formal Chern roots.

references.locator: §14, orientations of complex bundles and introduction to Chern classes

nodes.title: The Chern character, Todd and Â classes, and multiplicativity
nodes.statement: The Chern character is additive on direct sums, multiplicative on tensor products, and descends to complex K-groups. For formal Chern roots x_j, Td=∏_j x_j/(1−e^(−x_j)); Â is the multiplicative class expressed using Pontryagin roots. Every real vector bundle V satisfies Td(V⊗ℂ)=Â(V)² in rational cohomology, without an orientation hypothesis on V.

nodes.title: Cohomological Thom classes, Euler classes, and fiber integration
nodes.statement: An oriented real rank-r bundle π:V→X has a Thom class U∈Hʳ(V,V∖X;ℚ). The map Φ(a)=π*a∪U is the relative, equivalently fiberwise compact-support, Thom isomorphism, with inverse given by fiber integration. For classes compactly supported on the base, H_c^k(X)≅H_c^{k+r}(V). The zero section i satisfies i*U=e(V) and i*i!(a)=a∪e(V).

nodes.title: The Thom defect formula for the Chern character
nodes.statement: Define 𝔗(V)=π!ch(i!1). Then π!ch(i!u)=𝔗(V)ch(u). In the SG convention, if rank_ℂ V=k, then 𝔗(V)=(−1)^k Td(V̄)⁻¹.
nodes.scope_boundary: The sign and conjugate bundle are those of the specified SG exterior-algebra Thom class. The universal Euler-class argument is performed in the universal calculation, not by cancelling an Euler class on an arbitrary base where it may be a zero divisor.

nodes.title: The cohomological index formula as a pairing on TX
nodes.statement: Let X be compact without boundary, dim X=n, and P a complex elliptic operator. Then ind P=(−1)^n⟨ch[σ(P)]∪π*Â(TX)²,[TX]⟩. The tangent total space TX has the complex orientation locally specified by (x,ξ)↦x+iξ, ch[σ(P)] is compactly supported, and [TX] is the locally finite fundamental class. X itself need not be orientable.

references.locator: §2, Proposition (2.11) and Index Theorem (2.12), tangent-space cohomological index formula

scope_constraints: Cohomology is singular cohomology over ℚ, with the specified integral-to-rational normalization.
The cotangent symbol is transported to TX using the same Riemannian metric; the native tangent-chart complex orientation is used.
The factor (−1)^n belongs to the total-space orientation convention and is distinct from the base-formula permutation sign in T03.
No orientation of X, positive dimension, connectedness, nonempty-base, or equal source-target rank assumption is required.
nodes.scope_boundary: The formula includes the specified singular-cohomology and native Thom–Gysin model comparisons. It does not identify singular and Čech cohomology on arbitrary compact spaces, nor arbitrary independent differential-form or frame models.

nodes.title: The cohomological index formula as a pairing on the base manifold
nodes.statement: Let X be a compact oriented n-manifold without boundary and P a complex elliptic operator. Then ind P=(−1)^{n(n+1)/2}⟨π!ch[σ(P)]∪Â(TX)²,[X]⟩. Fiber integration π! is the inverse to the Thom map Φ(a)=π*a∪U. The sign compares the interleaved complex orientation on TX with the orientation having all base directions before all fiber directions.

references.locator: Second Theorem III.13.8, equation (13.24) and Note
§2, equation (2.13) and footnote 4, oriented-base index and Thom-order convention

scope_constraints: A compatible integral local homology orientation determines both the base fundamental class and the tangent-fiber Thom orientation.
The same Riemannian metric is used in the tangent Thom inverse and in transport of the original cotangent symbol.
The Thom order is π*a∪U. Its orientation permutation and the T02 total-space sign are retained separately before giving (−1)^{n(n+1)/2}.
The pairing is the finite top-degree characteristic-class sum; no positive dimension, even dimension, connectedness, nonempty-base, or equal source-target rank assumption is added.
nodes.scope_boundary: The selected singular-cohomology, integral orientation, and native tangent Thom–Gysin comparisons are part of the formula. General Čech, differential-form, or independent frame-model variants are separate statements.

nodes.title: Spin structures and chiral spinor bundles
nodes.statement: For an oriented Riemannian manifold, a spin structure consists of a principal Spin(n)-bundle and a Spin(n)→SO(n)-equivariant double covering of the oriented orthonormal frame bundle. In dimension n=2m, a complex Clifford spinor module with the specified volume-element grading defines S⁺ and S⁻. The chirality labels are fixed by this convention.

references.locator: II.1 and II.3, introductory spin constructions
§3.3, spin structures and lifted frame transition functions

nodes.scope_boundary: The native chiral spin-structure carrier is specified in positive even rank. The native rank-zero extension uses Spin(0)=1, a one-sheet frame lift, and the canonical empty orientation, rather than extending the positive-rank double-cover definition literally. The general literature definition in odd rank does not assert an additional odd-rank native chiral interface.

nodes.title: Twisted Dirac operators and their symbols
nodes.statement: On an even-dimensional spin manifold, equip a smooth complex bundle W with a Hermitian metric and a unitary connection. The spin connection and Clifford multiplication define D⁺_W:Γ(S⁺⊗W)→Γ(S⁻⊗W). With c(ξ)²=−|ξ|² and D_j=−i∂_j, the symbol is σ(D)(ξ)=i c(ξ). A homotopy removing the nonzero complex factor i identifies its symbol K-class with s(TX)·π*W.

references.locator: II.5, introductory Dirac construction and symbol
II.6, equations (6.1)–(6.14): positive chiral block and Clifford symbol

nodes.title: The K-theoretic Thom isomorphism for spin bundles
nodes.statement: For an even-rank spin bundle V over compact X, the spinor symbol s(V) is a K-orientation: multiplication by it gives K(X)≅K_c(V).

nodes.title: The Chern character of the spinor Thom class
nodes.statement: Let V be a real rank-2m spin bundle over a compact Hausdorff base. Using the orientation induced by that same spin structure for both its spinor Thom class and inverse Thom map, pi! ch s(V)=(-1)^m Ahat(V)^(-1). Tensoring with a coefficient bundle W multiplies the right side by ch(W).
nodes.source_scope_relation: This is the compact-base specialization of the spinor Thom formula; the prescribed spin structure fixes both orientation choices.

nodes.title: The twisted spin Dirac index formula
nodes.statement: Let X be a compact Riemannian spin manifold without boundary of dimension 2m, and W a finite-rank smooth complex bundle with a Hermitian metric and a smooth connection. In the SG chirality and induced orientation conventions, ind D+_W=<ch(W) cup Ahat(TX),[X]>. This includes the native zero-dimensional case and does not require the dimension to be divisible by four.

references.locator: §3.4, Theorem 3.4.4: the twisted spin Dirac index formula

scope_constraints: The operator is the actual positive chiral twisted Dirac operator for the same spin structure, metric, and coefficient bundle W.
The orientation of X is induced by that same spin structure and agrees with its Thom orientation.
The analytic index is defined by the kernel and cokernel of the original operator. Replacing the cokernel by ker D⁻_W requires an additional formal-adjoint identification.

Every even dimension, including the native zero-dimensional endpoint, is allowed. In dimension zero the operator is W→0 with the positive empty orientation. The specialized zero-dimensional theorem omits a connection parameter; the uniform even-dimensional interface retains the supplied coefficient connection and evaluates the Dirac operator as an empty tangent-basis sum.
The characteristic-class expression uses the actual Chern character of W and a finite top-degree cup-product sum.
nodes.scope_boundary: Curvature formulas, heat-kernel or spectral proofs, spin-c extensions, noncompact and boundary versions, and additional Poincaré-duality models are separate statements.
nodes.source_scope_relation: The usual unitary-connection version is included. Smooth connection changes affect only lower-order terms. SG II.1, Definition 1.3 and its following conventions treat positive ranks n≥3, n=2 and n=1, and give no rank-zero convention. The native zero-dimensional endpoint is proved separately in the project using Spin(0)=1 from the group generated by even products of unit vectors, the exterior-algebra model, and the positive empty-frame orientation. It evaluates the original empty tangent-basis operator with its native spin orientation; arbitrary signed or stabilized zero-dimensional models are outside this scope.

nodes.title: Symbol estimates for a cutoff inverse
nodes.statement: If an elliptic matrix symbol p∈S^m satisfies the inverse-symbol estimates, then q₀=χ(|ξ|)p⁻¹ belongs to S^{−m}.

nodes.title: Fredholmness from an inverse modulo compact operators
nodes.statement: If bounded operators T:H₁→H₂ and Q:H₂→H₁ satisfy QT=I−S₁ and TQ=I−S₂ with compact S₁ and S₂, then both T and Q are Fredholm.

nodes.title: A fixed finite-dimensional complement under Fredholm perturbations
nodes.statement: Let T₀ be Fredholm and V⊆H₁ closed of finite codimension with V∩ker T₀=0. Every sufficiently small perturbation T remains injective on V, has TV closed, and gives a natural isomorphism W=(T₀V)⊥≅H₂/TV. These quotient spaces form a locally trivial family.

nodes.title: The universal multiplicative identity for multiplicative sequences
nodes.statement: A multiplicative sequence F generated by a rational formal power series f with constant term one satisfies F(bc)=F(b)F(c) on the completion of 1 plus positive-degree elements of a commutative graded rational algebra.
nodes.source_scope_relation: The implemented algebra is ordinarily commutative; the grading does not introduce odd-degree sign rules.

nodes.title: The zero-section formula for the cohomological Thom map
nodes.statement: For an oriented real bundle V over compact X with zero section i, i*i!(a)=a∪e(V). In the even-rank case used here this also equals e(V)∪a, for the Thom convention π*a∪U.

nodes.title: The zero-section formula for the K-theoretic Thom element
nodes.statement: For a complex bundle E over a compact base, i*i!(a)=λ₋₁(E)·a, where λ₋₁(E)=[Λeven E]−[Λodd E].

nodes.title: Path connectedness of Fredholm operators of fixed index
nodes.statement: Two Fredholm operators between the same complex Hilbert spaces with equal index are joined by a norm-continuous path of Fredholm operators.

nodes.title: Path connectedness of the invertible group on a complex Hilbert space
nodes.statement: The group of bounded invertible operators on a complex Hilbert space is path connected in the norm topology.

nodes.title: Normalized loop representatives of relative K-classes
nodes.statement: Every class in K(X×B²,X×S¹), for compact X, is represented by a trivial-bundle triple d(T,T,α) with α(x,1)=I. Equality of such classes is expressed by homotopy of normalized loops after stabilization.

nodes.title: Finite projectivity of a shifted Laurent-loop cokernel
nodes.statement: For an invertible Laurent matrix loop σ, a sufficiently large positive shift σ_k=z^kσ acts on A⟨z⟩^n with finitely generated projective cokernel M(σ,k). For l≥0, M(σ,k+l)≅M(σ,k)⊕A^{nl}.

nodes.title: Reduction of a Laurent loop to a difference of polynomial loops
nodes.statement: In the stable loop group, [σ]=[z^kσ]−[z^k I], where k is chosen large enough that both loops are polynomial.

nodes.title: Stable degree reduction of polynomial loops
nodes.statement: Every invertible polynomial loop can be reduced, by stabilization and normalized homotopy, to an affine loop a₀+a₁z.

nodes.title: Fourier coefficient identities for the inverse of an affine loop
nodes.statement: If σ(z)=a₀+a₁z with a₀+a₁=I and τ=Σ_j b_jz^j=σ⁻¹, then a₀ and a₁ commute with every b_j and the coefficients b_i commute with one another. Between the negative and nonnegative Fourier parts, b_i a_ν b_j=b_i b_j=0 for i<0≤j and ν∈{0,1}.

nodes.title: Projection factorization of an affine loop
nodes.statement: With the notation of KL05, q=a₀b₀ is a projection and p=I−q. The factorization σ(z)=σ⁺(z)σ⁻(z⁻¹)(pz+q) has σ⁺ and σ⁻ invertible in the respective algebras of nonnegative and nonpositive absolutely summable series.

nodes.title: Square identities for exterior multiplication and contraction
nodes.statement: On the exterior algebra of a complex Hermitian vector space, ε_v²=ι_v²=0 and ε_vι_v+ι_vε_v=‖v‖²I. Consequently (ε_v+ι_v)²=‖v‖²I.

nodes.title: Asymptotic summation of symbols
nodes.statement: On an open coordinate domain, a sequence of local S^m_{1,0} symbols whose real orders decrease strictly to −∞ has an asymptotic sum, with estimates on each compact subset. On the specified compact-manifold quantization and operator model, two operators with the same asymptotic expansion differ by an infinitely smoothing operator.
nodes.literature_statement: A sequence of symbols with orders tending to −∞ has an asymptotic sum, unique modulo infinitely smoothing terms.
nodes.scope_boundary: Local symbol existence is stated on open coordinate domains with compact-subset estimates. Uniqueness modulo infinitely smoothing operators is stated for the specified compact-manifold operator model, not for arbitrary subsets U.

nodes.title: Rellich compactness
nodes.statement: A sequence supported in a fixed compact set and bounded in H^s has a subsequence convergent in H^{s′} for each s′<s.

nodes.title: Sobolev duality
nodes.statement: The integral pairing identifies H^{−s} with the continuous dual of H^s. The bundle version uses the density and the dual bundle.

nodes.title: From local Thom generators to a global Thom isomorphism
nodes.statement: For a complex bundle over a compact base, if its candidate Thom class gives an isomorphism on every graded K-group over the closed subsets of trivializing neighborhoods, then it gives a global Thom isomorphism.

nodes.title: The Chern character of the half-spinor difference
nodes.statement: For an even-rank real spin bundle V of rank 2m, the half-spinor difference satisfies ch(S⁺−S⁻)=(−1)^m e(V)Â(V)⁻¹ in the SG chirality convention.

nodes.title: Banach algebras and projective modules in the Bott proof
nodes.statement: The Bott proof uses A=C(X), the correspondence between finitely generated projective modules and vector bundles, loops in stable general linear groups, and algebras of absolutely summable power series, together with their specified model comparisons.

references.locator: III.1.5, 1.7–1.9, and 1.12–1.17, including their references to I.6 and II.2

nodes.title: Approximation by Laurent loops
nodes.statement: Stable homotopy classes of Laurent loops agree with the fundamental group classes of all continuous loops in the general linear group.

nodes.title: Homotopy invariance of projective modules over an interval
nodes.statement: The image modules at the two endpoints of a continuous family of projections p(t) are isomorphic.

nodes.title: The Bott map from projective modules to loops
nodes.statement: The rule γ([im p])=[z↦pz+I−p] defines a group homomorphism K(A)→π₁GL(A). For A=C(X), it agrees with multiplication by the two-dimensional Bott class.

nodes.title: A left inverse of the Bott loop map
nodes.statement: The rule γ′([σ])=[M(σ,k)]−[A^{nk}] is well defined and satisfies γ′γ=id. Hence γ is injective.

nodes.title: Surjectivity of the Bott loop map
nodes.statement: The Bott homomorphism γ:K(A)→π₁GL(A) is surjective.

nodes.title: Complex conjugation on low-dimensional equivariant Bott classes
nodes.statement: Let ψ be complex conjugation on V=W⊗ℂ. If W=ℝ and G=O(1), then ψ*a=−a·ξ, where ξ is the sign representation. If W=ℝ² and G=SO(2), then ψ*a=a.

nodes.title: The two-fixed-point decomposition of the sphere de Rham symbol
nodes.statement: For the standard O(r) action on Sʳ, ρ_{Sʳ}=j⁰_!1+θ*j∞_!1, where j⁰ and j∞ include the two fixed points and θ negates the tangent fibers.

nodes.title: Point normalization from low-dimensional de Rham and augmentation identities
nodes.statement: Suppose an index function satisfies excision, R(G)-linearity, and naturality under group restriction. If the SO(2)-equivariant de Rham index on S² is 2, the O(1)-equivariant de Rham index on S¹ is 1−ξ, and the ordinary circle point-pushforward index is 1, then the corresponding low-dimensional equivariant point-pushforward indices are 1.

nodes.title: Equivariant Bott classes, forward maps, and model compatibility
nodes.statement: For finite-dimensional continuous complex representations of compact Hausdorff groups, the exterior and Koszul models define equivariant Bott classes and R(G)-linear forward multiplication maps. Point-representation coefficients, the standard zero-dimensional model, independence of unitary coordinates, and compatibility with external products, group restriction, extension along open inclusions, and the SG exterior-algebra model are specified.

references.locator: §2, equation (2.7) and the prerequisites to Lemma (2.8)

nodes.literature_statement: For a finite-dimensional complex representation V of a compact group G, its equivariant Bott element generates K_{G,c}(V) as an R(G)-module. The associated isomorphism is compatible with external products, group restriction, and extension along open inclusions; its model is compared with the SG exterior-algebra triple.
nodes.scope_boundary: This node specifies the concrete class, forward maps, coefficient and zero-dimensional identifications, and naturality. The general equivariant Bott-generation theorem, bijectivity, and inverse are distinct from this scope; zero-dimensional bijectivity does not imply the general theorem.
scope_constraints: The unitary exterior-class construction and its forward-map identities also apply to a supplied continuous unitary action without compactness or Lie-group structure.
The compact Hausdorff hypothesis supplies invariant unitary coordinates for a general finite-dimensional continuous representation.

nodes.title: Equivariant de Rham indices of low-dimensional spheres
nodes.statement: The SO(2)-equivariant de Rham index on S² is 2, and the O(1)-equivariant de Rham index on S¹ is 1−ξ.

nodes.title: Direct Fourier normalization of a point pushforward on the circle
nodes.statement: For the exterior-algebra Thom convention in ASI, a point inclusion j into the circle has ordinary analytic index ind(j!1)=1.

nodes.title: Equivariant external-product index multiplicativity for different groups
nodes.statement: If G₁ and G₂ act on the respective factors, then ind_{G₁×G₂}(u⊠v)=ind_{G₁}(u)⊠ind_{G₂}(v).

references.locator: §4, external-product property; §9, its proof for the analytic index

nodes.title: From low-dimensional normalization to O(r)
nodes.statement: Excision, point normalization for O(1) and SO(2), and external-product multiplicativity for different groups imply that the point Bott index is 1 for every O(r).

nodes.title: Kernel and cokernel decomposition for graded product operators
nodes.statement: For the specified closed Sobolev realizations of elliptic operators P and Q, the graded product matrix D has kernel (ker P⊗ker Q)⊕(ker P*⊗ker Q*) and cokernel (ker P*⊗ker Q)⊕(ker P⊗ker Q*).

nodes.title: Local product-cutoff estimates and symbol homotopy
nodes.statement: For first-order symbols with fixed compact coordinate support, the SG cutoff ψ_ε(r,s)=1−φ(ε√(r²+s²))φ(εs/r) gives an H¹→L² error of order O(ε). For sufficiently small ε, the corresponding graded-symbol cutoff preserves the elliptic K-class.

references.locator: III.13.5, p.250: the cutoff left as an exercise

nodes.title: Two-sided localization for excision
nodes.statement: For a zero-order elliptic symbol equal to the identity outside a compact subset of the base, there is a representative equal to the identity outside a larger compact subset. The nonidentity parts of the Schwartz kernels of both P and P* have compact-support control in both variables.

nodes.title: The spinor-symbol triple of an even-rank spin bundle
nodes.statement: The spinor-symbol triple is s(V)=[π*S⁺,π*S⁻;c(v)], with c(v)²=−‖v‖² and c(v) invertible off the zero section. Over a compact base it defines a class in K_c(V).

nodes.title: Finite projectivity of a polynomial-multiplier cokernel
nodes.statement: Let f be a matrix polynomial invertible in the algebra of two-sided absolutely summable Laurent series, with inverse g. Multiplication by f on X=A⟨z⟩^n has a finitely generated projective A-module as its cokernel.

references.locator: III.1, Lemma 1.18: left-inverse construction and cokernel diagram

nodes.scope_boundary: The finite-projectivity argument uses the truncation correction of the left-inverse construction in Karoubi III.1 Lemma 1.18; this repair is a project supplement to the printed argument.

analysis_foundations.direct_project_consumers_scope: Handwritten source consumers, with intervening implementation details contracted; node consumers retain the registered mathematical scope.

groups.scope: The L2 Fourier transform is a complex-linear isometry equivalence for complete complex Hilbert-valued functions on a finite-dimensional real inner product space. Pointwise inversion retains its integrability and pointwise continuity hypotheses.

groups.topic: Completion, continuous duality, and Riesz representation
groups.scope: The completion uses the original uniform structure. Riesz representation is the conjugate-linear isometry equivalence for a complete inner product space, with the library's inner product convention.
The original Banach, continuous linearity, and surjectivity or bijectivity assumptions remain part of the library interfaces.
These interfaces supply abstract compact-operator composition properties. They are not the geometric Rellich theorem.
Rank-nullity and the formula index equals source dimension minus target dimension refer to the original linear map and finite-dimensional spaces.
